name: Environment Configuration Best Practices
description: This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building environment configuration — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary environment configuration tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.
content:
This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building environment configuration — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary environment configuration tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Re-check edge cases relevant to environment configuration (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
2. When environment configuration guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
3. Document any non-obvious environment configuration decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
4. Surface known limitations of a chosen environment configuration approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
5. When environment configuration decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
6. Keep environment configuration changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
7. Keep environment configuration outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
8. Prefer the simplest environment configuration approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
9. When multiple environment configuration strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
10. State assumptions about environment configuration explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
11. Validate environment configuration outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
12. Check that environment configuration terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of environment configuration correctness.
- Do not silently drop environment configuration edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not apply generic environment configuration advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid introducing new environment configuration abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about environment configuration over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
